title: Enterprise Cloud Migration and Modernization Services
_provenance: DERIVED MOCK — no PRC-001 pricing capture exists for opp-001. Synthesized 2026-06-11 from opp-001-strategy.json (pricingStrategy: PTW $42.0M, LPTA floor $38M, blended/competitive rates, 22% margin), opp-001-teaming.json (workshareAllocation: $45.0M ceiling, prime 55% / subs 20/15/10), and opp-001-staffing.json (LCAT labor basis — the ROM live-link). Pending Greg ratification. Never present as live agent output.

overview.note: Two estimates frame the price: a top-down Price-to-Win ($42.0M, competitive analysis) and a bottom-up Build-Up ($44.2M, cost+fee). The $2.2M gap is closed via the fee, overhead, and subcontractor-negotiation levers to a proposed $42.8M — above PTW for margin protection, below build-up via the identified levers.

topDown.label: Price-to-Win (competitive)
topDown.basis: Derived from 8 comparable DHS OCIO cloud awards (FY23–25), GSA CALC+ rate benchmarks, and the incumbent's public billing rate. Positions the bid to win on best-value while undercutting incumbent labor rates.
sources: USAspending — 8 comparable DHS OCIO awards FY23–25

bottomUp.label: Cost Build-Up (engineering estimate)
bottomUp.basis: Built from the staffing labor basis (15 prime FTE across 6 LCATs, 5-year escalated), fully-burdened with fringe/overhead/G&A/fee, plus subcontractor costs ($20.25M) and ODCs. Represents the cost to deliver the proposed solution.

neck.recommendation: Close the $2.2M build-up-to-PTW gap with: (1) fee reduction from 8% to 7% on the prime portion (~$0.25M), (2) overhead efficiency from the existing FedRAMP environment reuse (~$0.6M), (3) subcontractor cost negotiation on the two unsigned TAs (~$1.0M target), and (4) ODC tightening (~$0.35M). Hold proposed at $42.8M to protect the 22% margin while remaining competitive.

fair.facts: Target Price-to-Win: $42.0M against a $45.0M ceiling. Contract type: FFP base year, T&M option years. Competitive position: undercut the incumbent on labor rate while leading on best-value (FedRAMP High, same-agency past performance). Senior-labor blended rate $185/hr vs. the incumbent's public $195/hr; full-program blended rate ~$131/hr.
fair.analysis: PTW is anchored on 8 comparable DHS OCIO cloud awards (FY23–25) and GSA CALC+ benchmarks. The $42.0M target sits ~6.7% under the ceiling, signaling price discipline without bidding into LPTA territory. Best-value evaluation (M.1–M.3) means TechForward does not need to be the lowest price — it needs to be the lowest credible price among technically-superior offerors, which the FedRAMP High and same-agency discriminators support.
fair.intelligence: 🔒 Incumbent Peraton's expiring agency ATO forces a re-authorization cost that TechForward does not carry — a structural price advantage of roughly 4–6 weeks of program ramp that competitors without an active ATO must price in. The $185/hr senior rate vs. $195/hr incumbent rate is a defensible, public-data-grounded undercut.
fair.recommendations: PR-1-R1: Set Price-to-Win target at $42.0M. · PR-1-R2: Hold senior-labor rate at $185/hr to undercut the incumbent on the visible band. · PR-1-R3: Do not bid below the $38M LPTA floor unless the solicitation converts to LPTA (see PR-5).

envelope.aiReasoning: PTW rests on 8 comparable awards plus public rate data, which is a solid competitive basis; confidence is held below the 80s only because the LPTA-vs-best-value evaluation methodology is not yet confirmed in the draft solicitation, and that choice materially shifts the target.

fair.facts: Bottom-up build-up: $44.2M total (5-year). Cost elements: Direct labor (prime) $12.8M · Fringe & overhead $7.9M · Subcontractor costs $20.25M · Other direct costs (travel, cloud, tools) $1.5M · G&A $1.1M · Fee/profit $0.65M.
fair.analysis: Direct labor is built from the staffing LCAT basis (15 prime FTE, 6 categories, midpoint salaries, 3% annual escalation across 5 years — see PR-3). Subcontractor costs flow from the teaming workshare allocation ($9.0M / $6.75M / $4.5M). The build-up exceeds PTW by $2.2M; the hourglass neck documents the levers to close it. Fee is set at 8% on the prime portion, trimmable to 7% as the first lever.
fair.intelligence: 🔒 The single largest cost line is subcontractor cost ($20.25M, 46% of build-up), which is also the least locked — two of three subcontractor TAs are unsigned (see PR-4). Cost certainty improves materially once those TAs are executed; until then the build-up carries a ±$1.0M band on the subcontractor portion.
fair.recommendations: PR-2-R1: Confirm the $44.2M build-up as the cost baseline. · PR-2-R2: Reduce prime fee from 8% to 7% as the first gap-closing lever. · PR-2-R3: Apply FedRAMP-environment-reuse overhead efficiency (~$0.6M) before pricing the option years.

envelope.aiReasoning: The build-up structure is sound and the labor basis is real (linked to staffing), but two assumptions cap confidence: the 3% escalation across the option years, and the ±$1.0M band on subcontractor costs from the unsigned TAs. Both resolve as the team locks.

fair.facts: Prime direct labor basis — 15 FTE across 6 LCATs (escalated 5-year extended cost contributes $12.8M to the build-up): LCAT-01 Program Manager (1 FTE, base $197.5K) · LCAT-02 Technical Lead / Cloud Architect (1 FTE, $222.5K) · LCAT-03 Cloud Architect — Migration (2 FTE, $175K) · LCAT-04 Security Engineer (3 FTE, $185K) · LCAT-05 DevOps Engineer (4 FTE, $147.5K) · LCAT-06 Systems Administrator (4 FTE, $105K). Rates are midpoints of the Staffing compensation ranges.
fair.analysis: This section is live-linked to the Staffing tab: FTE counts and compensation ranges flow from the staffing LCAT data, so a staffing change (added position, candidate at a different rate band, or a position lost) re-flows the labor cost here automatically. Fully-burdened, the 15 prime FTE carry ~$170K/FTE/year direct, wrapped with fringe and overhead in PR-2.
fair.intelligence: 🔒 The Program Manager (Angela Rodriguez, committed, Exceptional CPARS) and Technical Lead are priced at the top of band intentionally — their qualifications are proposal discriminators, and underpricing Key Personnel signals weakness to evaluators. Commodity positions (DevOps, SysAdmin) are priced at midpoint for competitiveness.
fair.recommendations: PR-3-R1: Confirm the LCAT rate card at compensation midpoints. · PR-3-R2: Keep the Staffing live-link active — do not hardcode labor cost; it must re-flow if staffing changes. · PR-3-R3: Validate the 3% escalation assumption against current federal labor market data before submission.

envelope.aiReasoning: Labor is the most defensible cost line because it traces directly to named candidates and real compensation ranges in Staffing. Confidence is high; the only open variable is escalation across the option years.

fair.facts: Subcontractor costs total $20.25M (46% of build-up): DataBridge Analytics — Data Migration & ETL — $9.0M (20% workshare) · GovFlow Technologies — ServiceNow & ITSM — $6.75M (15%) · MainframeNext Inc. — Mainframe Modernization — $4.5M (10%).
fair.analysis: Subcontractor pricing is carried at the teaming workshare allocation. Two of the three TAs are unsigned (GovFlow at term sheet, MainframeNext NDA in legal review), so $11.25M of the $20.25M is not yet locked. The DataBridge figure ($9.0M) is the most firm (verbal commitment, TA in legal review) but is the single largest subcontractor line and the primary target of the cost-negotiation lever.
fair.intelligence: 🔒 Competitor pressure (CACI/Vertex contacted DataBridge and GovFlow) limits negotiating leverage on those two — pushing too hard on price risks losing them to a competing team. MainframeNext, a smaller firm, has more pricing flexibility but unconfirmed capacity.
fair.recommendations: PR-4-R1: Negotiate ~$1.0M aggregate reduction across subcontractor costs as the largest gap-closing lever — but protect DataBridge and GovFlow relationships against competitor poaching. · PR-4-R2: Lock subcontractor pricing only on TA execution. · PR-4-R3: Hold an alternate-partner pricing scenario (MigrationPro/Attain for CG-01) in case DataBridge does not sign.

envelope.aiReasoning: This is the weakest-locked and largest cost line: $11.25M of $20.25M sits behind unsigned TAs, and competitor interest caps negotiating room. Confidence reflects real, unresolved cost risk — appropriately the lowest section on the tab.

fair.facts: Margin target: 22% overall. Proposed price $42.8M (above the $42.0M PTW for margin protection). LPTA contingency floor: $38.0M. Dual pricing model maintained: best-value primary, LPTA fallback.
fair.analysis: The proposed $42.8M protects the 22% margin while closing most of the build-up gap via the documented levers. If the solicitation converts to LPTA (a live risk flagged in the risk register), the fallback model strips to the $38.0M floor — achieved by reducing fee, descoping option-year ODCs, and applying the maximum subcontractor-cost negotiation. Below $38.0M the bid is not viable without margin erosion past acceptable thresholds.
fair.intelligence: 🔒 The LPTA-vs-best-value methodology is the single largest pricing unknown. Industry-day signals lean best-value, but DHS OCIO has used LPTA for commodity-heavy scopes. Pricing both models now avoids a fire-drill re-price if the final RFP confirms LPTA.
fair.recommendations: PR-5-R1: Set proposed price at $42.8M with the 22% margin. · PR-5-R2: Maintain the dual best-value / LPTA model; do not collapse to a single number until the evaluation methodology is confirmed. · PR-5-R3: Treat $38.0M as the absolute floor — escalate any pressure to bid lower.

envelope.aiReasoning: Margin strategy is sound and the dual model is the right hedge, but confidence is capped by the unconfirmed evaluation methodology — the LPTA-vs-best-value choice swings the entire pricing posture and is not yet knowable from the draft solicitation.
